expert_derived.note: Kernels whose design is AWS's, not found by any arm. Not search discoveries.

aws_as_shipped.what: kernels/matmul_expert.py: AWS's SDK 2.32 tutorial matmul (caps 16/2/8, P2's fp32 accumulation fix). It is attempt 0 of every random-search run: 2.493x, 2.490x and 2.496x vs start there; 385.6 us is the sweep's record for it.

aws_as_published.what: kernels/matmul_expert_aws.py: AWS's bf16 K-block accumulation, 5.3 bf16 ulps (limit 4)

lnc2.label: not a referee verdict
lnc2.what: P2 engineering on the expert: kernels/matmul_expert_lnc2.py launched as kernel[2] on both physical cores, caps m2 n6 k16. Timed by P1's timer with the referee's correctness check at the timing shapes. Not a referee verdict.
lnc2.caps_from: the best of the archived first random-search run (older referee, not counted in arm c); the sweep ranks m2 n6 k16 6 of 62
lnc2.breakdown: 960.5 us -> 385.6 (AWS's design, 2.49x) -> 288.3 (block sizes m2 n6 k16 at LNC=1, 1.34x) -> 192.2 (the second physical core, 1.50x)

search_discovered.note: Found by arm c (random search over the expert's three block caps), attempts 1-23 of each run. x_over_expert is the best's speedup over that run's own attempt 0 (the expert as shipped, same session), both speedups from the referee's A/B against start: the dashboard's tuning study computes the same. search.py --summarize prints it from the logs.
search_discovered.busy_core_fix: The runs used search.py from before the busy-core fix (e369e5f, now merged here). It would not have changed them: every run logged its full budget, attempts 0-23, so no candidate was skipped.

ground_truth_sweep.note: Every SBUF-fitting setting timed once (search.py --exhaustive, logs/seat-102/sweep-*.jsonl): a measurement of the space, not a discovery by any arm.
ground_truth_sweep.aws_default_rank: m2 n2 k8 (the expert as shipped), 29 of 62

detail.measured: 2026-10-10, seat-102, branch kernels-search. Matmul start/expert 13:25; arm c, the sweep and LNC=2 15:00-15:30 on P1's referee 76b2227. RMSNorm/copy at 2048 tokens 13:55.
detail.times_are: the sum over each op's time_shapes in shapes.py, the same sum the referee's speedup uses

matmul.expert: kernels/matmul_expert.py: AWS's SDK 2.32 fully optimised tutorial matmul, accumulating K-blocks in fp32. Correct on 8 chip shapes, worst 0.50 bf16 ulps.
matmul.expert_as_published: kernels/matmul_expert_aws.py: same kernel with AWS's bf16 K-block accumulation. Referee verdict WRONG: 5.3 bf16 ulps at K=2048 (limit 4).
matmul.floor: not measured: no matmul floor is claimed

rmsnorm.floor: kernels/copy_floor.py: the same bytes copied through SBUF, rows packed into partitions in >= 2 overlapping chunks. Against the one-tile-per-DMA copy (kernels/copy_tiled.py): 89.7 vs 91.3 us at 2048x4096, 51.1 vs 344.2 us at 32768x128 (256-byte rows).
rmsnorm.room: start / floor = 1.82x at input_layernorm, 6.95x at q_norm, 3.68x on the sum

history_256_tokens.why_replaced: at 256 tokens a 4 MiB copy took ~20 us, mostly the ~17 us launch cost
